critique.evidence: Desktop is polished and cohesive: the oversized headline, restrained cyan/green/yellow palette, crisp dividers, and asymmetric evidence panel create a convincing technical-editorial hierarchy. Tablet remains composed, but becomes vertically long. Mobile is substantially weaker: tiny uppercase labels, dense stacked rows, awkward headline wrapping, and similarity values detached beneath each record reduce scanability. The actual tablet/mobile headers visibly clip navigation text and hide later destinations; the mobile header also loses the wordmark and red-mode action, making it feel compressed rather than intentionally adapted.
critique.fix: Redesign the compact header with an explicit menu or condensed section indicator; increase mobile label/body legibility; tighten the precedent rows by aligning similarity with each record; and rebalance mobile spacing and headline scale to reduce the excessively tall, fragmented composition.
